# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: mu = 0 vs H1: mu > 0 (one-sided, right-tailed)
# Parameters:
# n = 25 participants
# effect_size = 0.2 units (unstandardized mean difference)
# sd = 0.5 units (standard deviation)
# alpha = 0.05 (significance level)
# one-sided test

library(stats)

n <- 25
effect_size_mean <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
null_mean <- 0

# Calculate Cohen's d (standardized effect size)
cohens_d <- effect_size_mean / sd

# Non-centrality parameter for t-distribution
# lambda = (effect_size / sd) * sqrt(n) = Cohen's d * sqrt(n)
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n - 1

# For one-sided test (right-tailed), get critical t-value
# Critical value at alpha = 0.05
t_critical <- qt(p = 1 - alpha, df = df)

# Power = P(T > t_critical | H1 is true)
# This is the cumulative probability in the non-central t-distribution
power <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df = df, ncp = ncp)

# Round to reasonable precision
power_rounded <- round(power, 4)

  alternative = "greater",
  type = "one.sample"
)
